beats.text: Near the palace Odysseus sees his old dog Argos lying neglected on dung.
Argos lifts his head, drops his ears, and wags his tail at the scent and voice of his master.
Odysseus turns aside to hide a tear while asking Eumaeus about the animal.
After twenty years Argos dies as soon as he has recognized Odysseus.

figures.q: an old dog lying down
a thin old hound

sign.name: Mark
sign.operation: Matched mediums of the beggar's hand at each table, same framing.

key_beat.note: the king begging in his own hall

beats.text: Eumaeus enters first and Telemachus signals him to seat the beggar at the door.
Odysseus crosses his own threshold unrecognized and hears Phemius singing.
He begs from suitor to suitor to test each man's character.
Most give food while Antinous demands to know who admitted him.

figures.q: a beggar with a staff
a seated musician playing a lyre

sign.name: Imprint
sign.operation: Pose-to-pose: the stool's arc, the hit, his body unmoved; close on the silent vow.

key_beat.note: I had a house and men of my own once

beats.text: Odysseus tells a false story of former wealth and Egyptian disaster to Antinous.
Antinous insults him and orders him away from the table.
The beggar answers boldly; Antinous hurls a footstool into his shoulder.
Odysseus does not stagger and silently prays for Antinous's death.
Even the other suitors condemn the violation of a stranger.

figures.q: a small wooden footstool on floor

sign.name: Plastic figure
sign.operation: Hold on Penelope laughing at the sound.

key_beat.note: they struck a guest in my own house

beats.text: Penelope hears of the beggar's endurance and asks Eumaeus to bring him for questioning.
Odysseus delays until dusk, saying the suitors may attack him in the open hall.
Penelope praises the stranger's caution and asks that he come when the room empties.
Telemachus sneezes loudly; Penelope reads it as an omen that the suitors will die.

figures.q: a veiled woman seated by a window

sign.name: Bodies of attitude
sign.operation: Static wide of the night hall.

key_beat.note: the pigs want me before dawn

beats.text: At night Eumaeus prepares to return to the farm and asks Telemachus for instructions.
Telemachus tells him to come back at dawn with news.
Eumaeus takes leave of the disguised Odysseus and the prince without recognizing their bond.
The beggar remains in the palace under the suitors' gaze.

figures.q: a beggar seated by a doorway

sign.name: Theatrical figure
sign.operation: Frontal ring of suitors.

beats.text: The palace beggar Irus arrives and tries to drive Odysseus from the threshold.
They trade insults while the suitors gather, delighted by the prospect of a fight.
Antinous offers food and privileged access to the winner.
Odysseus makes the suitors swear that no one will strike him from behind.

figures.q: a fat beggar in rags

sign.name: Theatrical figure
sign.operation: Stage it as a ring of suitors, frontal and theatrical; the blow on twos; the suitors cheering their own doom.

beats.text: Odysseus tucks up his rags and reveals powerful thighs and shoulders.
Athena enlarges his appearance; Irus trembles but is forced into the ring.
Odysseus chooses not to kill him and breaks his jaw with one compact blow.
He drags Irus to the gate and warns him not to return.
The suitors cheer and Amphinomus gives the victor food and wine.

figures.q: a bare-chested strongman flexing muscles
a boxer knocked down

sign.name: Limit of the large form action-image
sign.operation: Hold Amphinomus walking away, shaken.

beats.text: Odysseus drinks to Amphinomus and warns that no man should become lawless in prosperity.
He predicts that Odysseus will return before the suitor can leave the palace.
Amphinomus walks away shaken, sensing danger but unable to escape Athena's design.
The warning becomes another unheeded exit offered before the slaughter.

figures.q: a two-handled wine cup raised

sign.name: Index of equivocity
sign.operation: Hold the wide of her descent with the veil and two maids; cut to Odysseus's face reading it one way and the suitors reading it another.

beats.text: Athena places a desire in Penelope to appear before the suitors and inflame their gifts.
She puts the queen to sleep, beautifies her, and wakes her radiant.
Penelope descends with two maids and rebukes Telemachus for allowing the stranger's abuse.
She recounts Odysseus's parting instructions and demands courtship gifts.
The suitors send for jewels, robes, and ornaments while Odysseus silently rejoices at her strategy.

figures.q: a veiled woman on a staircase
two young maidservants in robes
jewellery on a tray

sign.name: Binomial
sign.operation: Shot/reverse.

beats.text: After Penelope withdraws, disloyal maids light the hall for the suitors.
Melantho insults the beggar; he warns that the master may return.
Eurymachus mocks the beggar's baldness and offers him labor only to belittle him.
Odysseus answers with a challenge of work and war; Eurymachus throws a stool and misses.
Telemachus rebukes the suitors and ends the night's disorder.

figures.q: a young maid with a torch
a brazier burning at night

sign.name: Any-space-whatever
sign.operation: Dark wide of the hall with a light that has no visible source; the figures carrying arms small.

key_beat.note: keep the women shut in until this is done

beats.text: After the suitors depart, Odysseus tells Telemachus to remove the weapons from the hall.
Athena carries a golden lamp while father and son take shields, spears, and helmets to the storeroom.
Telemachus tells Eurycleia the smoke has damaged them and they must be protected from drunken quarrels.
The hall is left apparently defenseless for the future contest.

figures.q: a man carrying a round shield
a bundle of spears

sign.name: Mark
sign.operation: The same overhead loom framing as II-S02.

beats.text: Penelope comes down to the hearth and orders Melantho to stop insulting the guest.
She asks the beggar who he is, but he resists naming his lineage before hearing her grief.
Penelope describes the suitors and the shroud deception.
She asks for proof that the stranger truly knows Odysseus.

figures.q: a woman at a loom

sign.name: Powers of the false
sign.operation: Close, straight to Penelope, a face-to-camera telling; do not mark truth or falsehood.

beats.text: Odysseus invents the Cretan name Aethon and claims to have hosted Odysseus before Troy.
He describes the king's purple cloak, golden brooch, tunic, and herald Eurybates in exact detail.
Penelope weeps as if melting snow while Odysseus keeps his eyes hard despite inward grief.
She verifies the details and accepts that the stranger truly encountered her husband.
He swears Odysseus is near and will return within the month.

figures.q: a woman crying into her hands
an ornate gold brooch

sign.name: Index of lack
sign.operation: Close on the old hands washing, then the scar under them; she drops the foot.

beats.text: Penelope orders Eurycleia to wash the stranger's feet because his age resembles Odysseus's.
Odysseus recognizes the danger but cannot refuse without suspicion.
The nurse touches the old boar scar and instantly knows him.
She drops the foot into the basin, spilling water, and reaches toward Penelope.
Odysseus grips her throat gently but firmly and makes her swear silence.

figures.q: an old woman kneeling with a basin
a scar on a man's leg

sign.name: Strong destiny
sign.operation: Dissolve into the hunt, warm and slower frame rate; dissolve back to Eurycleia's hand.

beats.text: The scar triggers the story of young Odysseus visiting his grandfather Autolycus.
At dawn he hunts with his uncles on Mount Parnassus.
A boar bursts from dense cover and charges.
Odysseus spears it but receives a deep tusk wound above the knee.
The hunters bind the wound, stop the blood with a charm, and carry him home.

figures.q: a wild boar in the woods
a hunter with a spear
a pack of hunting dogs

sign.name: Rich dream
sign.operation: Dissolve into the dream, double exposure: twenty geese, the eagle, the voice of Odysseus.

key_beat.note: she sets the contest that ends it

beats.text: After the secret is restored, Penelope tells the beggar her dream of twenty geese killed by a great eagle.
In the dream the eagle speaks with Odysseus's voice and says the geese are the suitors.
Odysseus insists the dream has one unavoidable meaning.
Penelope announces the bow contest: she will marry the man who strings Odysseus's bow and shoots through twelve axes.
She withdraws upstairs and Athena gives her sleep.

figures.q: an eagle with spread wings
a flock of geese
a single white goose walking

sign.name: Bodies of attitude
sign.operation: Static on the portico.

key_beat.note: put your arrow in my breast tonight

beats.text: Odysseus lies awake in the portico, angered by disloyal maids slipping out to the suitors.
Athena appears and asks why he doubts after reaching home.
She promises protection even against many enemies and gives him sleep.
Upstairs Penelope wakes, prays for death, and dreams that Odysseus lies beside her.

figures.q: a man sleeping on the ground

sign.name: Plastic figure
sign.operation: Insert of clear sky with thunder.

beats.text: Before dawn Odysseus asks Zeus for a double sign from sky and household.
Zeus thunders from a clear sky.
A weary mill woman hears it and prays that the suitors' next feast be their last.
Odysseus recognizes both signs and takes courage.

figures.q: a woman at a quern
a round stone hand mill

sign.name: Vector
sign.operation: Wide of the court with pigs, goats and cattle entering from three sides.

key_beat.note: mark what I say, and let the gods hear it

beats.text: Eurycleia wakes the household and servants prepare the hall for Apollo's feast day.
Eumaeus arrives with pigs and greets the beggar kindly.
Melanthius enters with goats and renews his abuse.
Philoetius brings cattle, takes the stranger's hand, and weeps because he resembles Odysseus.
Odysseus predicts the master's return before the herdsman leaves.

figures.q: a herd of pigs
a flock of goats
cattle being led by rope

sign.name: Binomial
sign.operation: Shot/reverse.

key_beat.note: be glad you missed

beats.text: The suitors debate killing Telemachus, but an eagle with a dove appears on the left and Amphinomus rejects immediate action.
At the meal Ctesippus mocks the beggar and hurls an ox hoof as a guest-gift.
Odysseus dodges; Telemachus threatens to spear the offender if another assault occurs.
Agelaus challenges Telemachus over Penelope, but the prince refuses to control her choice.

figures.q: a hawk in flight overhead
a white dove in flight

sign.name: Peaks of the present
sign.operation: One wide of the feast with walls running with blood and shades in the doorway, not marked as vision; the suitors keep laughing.

beats.text: Athena drives the suitors into uncontrollable laughter while their meat drips blood in their vision.
Their faces distort and tears run beneath the laughter.
Theoclymenus sees darkness covering them, ghosts crowding the court, and blood on the walls.
He announces their approaching destruction and leaves when they mock him.
Telemachus and Odysseus watch one another across the doomed feast.

figures.q: a man laughing with head back

sign.name: Symbol
sign.operation: Insert of the bow in its case as the storeroom doors swing (the bolt shot back, the doors bellowing); her hands lift it into a shaft of light; hold on the bow across her lap.

beats.text: Athena inspires Penelope to begin the contest that will expose the suitors to slaughter.
The queen enters the storeroom, unlocks the doors, and lifts Odysseus's bow and quiver down.
She sits with the weapon across her knees and weeps before carrying it to the hall.
Two maids bring the chest of axes and set the implements before the suitors.

figures.q: a bow and quiver
a woman sitting with a bow across her lap

sign.name: Mark
sign.operation: Low wide straight down the trench so the twelve axe-head rings stack into one tunnel; then three matched mediums of Telemachus bending the bow, same lens, same length.

key_beat.note: here is the great bow of Odysseus

beats.text: Penelope announces that she will marry whoever strings the bow and shoots through all twelve axes.
Eumaeus and Philoetius weep at the sight of their master's weapon; Antinous rebukes them.
Telemachus plants the axes in a straight line and tries the bow three times.
On the fourth attempt he nearly strings it, but Odysseus signals him to stop.

figures.q: a man bending a bow
a row of axes

sign.name: Mark
sign.operation: Matched mediums, one per suitor (Leiodes, then two more, then Eurymachus), same framing on the bow, same cut length; the grease and fire shown between terms.

beats.text: Leiodes tries first, cannot bend the bow, and predicts it will destroy many suitors.
One after another the men strain, sweat, and fail.
Melanthius lights a fire and brings fat so the bow can be warmed and greased.
Even Eurymachus cannot string it and suffers humiliation.
Antinous postpones the contest for Apollo's festival feast.

figures.q: a man straining with a bow
a pot of grease on a fire

sign.name: Index of lack
sign.operation: In the outer yard, Odysseus draws the rag from his thigh; insert of the scar; the two herdsmen's faces; then the embrace.

key_beat.note: carry the bow to me anyway

beats.text: Odysseus follows Eumaeus and Philoetius outside and tests their loyalty.
He reveals the scar and declares that he is Odysseus.
The herdsmen embrace him and weep, then swear support.
Odysseus assigns Eumaeus to deliver the bow, Philoetius to lock the courtyard gate, and both to secure the women.

figures.q: two men embracing and weeping

sign.name: Binomial
sign.operation: Wide from the side with the bow in the middle ground; shot/reverse on one axis between Antinous and the beggar.

key_beat.note: no guest is refused in my house

beats.text: Back in the hall Odysseus asks to test his strength with the bow.
The suitors erupt in anger and fear that a beggar may succeed.
Penelope insists the stranger deserves a try and promises clothing and weapons if he wins.
Telemachus takes authority over the bow and orders his mother upstairs.
Eumaeus carries the bow through the shouting crowd to Odysseus.

figures.q: a man holding a bow

sign.name: Vector
sign.operation: Cross-cut three actions, each in its own framing (a door bar, the cable knot, the bow in hands); each cut leaves a gap the next fills; end on the wide of the closed hall.

beats.text: Eurycleia locks the women into their quarters at Telemachus's instruction.
Philoetius fastens the courtyard gate with a ship's cable.
Odysseus turns the bow in his hands, inspecting every part while the suitors mock him.
The hidden allies take their assigned positions and the escape routes close.

figures.q: a coiled ship's rope
a wooden door bar

sign.name: Demark
sign.operation: Frame the stringing with the row of failed suitors seated behind him: the norm and the aberration in one shot; no cut until the string is on.

key_beat.note: the stranger has not disgraced you — the turn

beats.text: Odysseus strings the bow effortlessly, as a musician strings a lyre.
He plucks the string and it sings like a swallow; Zeus answers with thunder.
Telemachus places sword and spear beside him and moves to his father's side.
Odysseus nocks an arrow and shoots cleanly through all twelve axes.
He tells Telemachus that the stranger has not disgraced the house and signals the next phase.

figures.q: a man drawing a bow
an arrow in flight

sign.name: Binomial
sign.operation: Low wide from behind Odysseus on the threshold into the hall; reverse from the hall at the figure in the doorway; Antinous's cup on the axis.

key_beat.note: you dogs. you never thought I would come home

beats.text: Odysseus strips off his rags, leaps onto the threshold, and pours the remaining arrows before him.
He shoots Antinous through the throat while the suitor lifts a cup.
Antinous falls across the table, spilling food and wine as the room erupts.
The suitors assume an accident and search for weapons that are no longer there.
Odysseus names himself and accuses them of consuming his house and violating his servants.

figures.q: an archer shooting from a doorway
a metal drinking cup on table

sign.name: Binomial
sign.operation: Shot/reverse on one axis for the bargain; then a wide as the tables rise as shields and the charge comes along the axis.

key_beat.note: my hands would not stop

beats.text: Eurymachus blames Antinous and offers repayment many times over if Odysseus spares them.
Odysseus rejects compensation and promises no survivor can escape his rage.
Eurymachus rallies the suitors to rush the archer beneath raised tables.
Odysseus shoots Eurymachus in the chest; Amphinomus charges and Telemachus kills him with a spear.

figures.q: a man throwing a spear

sign.name: Vector
sign.operation: Cross-cut Odysseus firing with Telemachus running the side passage; insert the storeroom door left open as he leaves.

beats.text: Telemachus runs to the storeroom and brings shields, helmets, and spears for Odysseus, Eumaeus, Philoetius, and himself.
He admits leaving the door unbarred after one trip.
The defenders arm in formation while Odysseus continues firing.
When the arrows run low they transition to spear combat.

figures.q: a man in a helmet with a shield

sign.name: Vector
sign.operation: Track Melanthius through the side passage and back with spears; cut to the herdsmen setting out after him; end on him hoisted to the rafters.

key_beat.note: someone is arming them out of my own storeroom

beats.text: Melanthius discovers the open storeroom route and carries weapons to the suitors.
Odysseus sees the enemy suddenly armed and orders Eumaeus and Philoetius to investigate.
They catch Melanthius returning for more arms.
They bind his hands and feet, hoist him by a rope to the rafters, and leave him suspended in pain.

figures.q: a man hanging by a rope

sign.name: Binomial
sign.operation: Wide on one axis: the suitors' throw, the spears turned into doors and walls, the defenders' reply.

key_beat.note: Mentor, keep ruin off me

beats.text: Athena enters in Mentor's form; Odysseus challenges her for delaying aid.
She rebukes him but first tests his strength by remaining disguised and partially withholding help.
The suitors throw spears; Athena deflects them into walls and doors.
The defenders answer with a coordinated volley and kill several men.
Athena raises her aegis from the roof beam and terror breaks the remaining formation.

figures.q: a spear thrown through the air
an owl on a beam

sign.name: Symptom
sign.operation: Pose-to-pose at 12 fps: the pursuit through the hall, Leiodes's head falling mid-plea, no cut away.

beats.text: Odysseus and his allies pursue the suitors through the hall like falcons among smaller birds.
Leiodes clasps Odysseus's knees but is killed despite claiming innocence.
Phemius and Medon appeal for mercy and Telemachus confirms their limited complicity.
Odysseus spares the bard and herald and orders them into the courtyard.
The living search the blood-filled hall for any remaining threat.

figures.q: a falcon diving on small birds
a man with a lyre

sign.name: Symptom
sign.operation: Pose-to-pose, the line of hanged figures in silhouette.

key_beat.note: twelve of you went the shameless way

beats.text: Eurycleia identifies twelve maids who consorted with the suitors and mocked the household.
The women are forced to carry bodies outside and clean the hall with water and sponges.
Telemachus rejects a clean sword death and hangs them together from a cable in the courtyard.
Melanthius is lowered, mutilated, and killed.
The household's corrupted labor system is violently purged.

figures.q: a woman scrubbing a floor
a bucket and sponge

sign.name: Bodies of gest
sign.operation: Frontal wide of Odysseus carrying the sulphur fire through the hall, the women entering in a line, each embracing him.

key_beat.note: not aloud — it is not holy to crow over dead men

beats.text: Odysseus orders Eurycleia to bring sulfur and fire so the hall can be purified.
Loyal women enter, recognize him, and embrace him in tears.
Odysseus receives them while restraining grief and maintaining security.
He sends Eurycleia upstairs to wake Penelope and announce that her husband has returned.

figures.q: a brazier of fire

sign.name: Index of equivocity
sign.operation: Two-shot at the bed, Penelope and Eurycleia; Penelope's face turns from the nurse to the door, undecided; hold.

key_beat.note: wake and see it with your own eyes

beats.text: Eurycleia wakes Penelope and says Odysseus has returned and killed the suitors.
Penelope first thinks the nurse has gone mad or that a god punished the men.
Eurycleia offers the scar as proof and describes the king waiting below.
Penelope descends, divided between embracing him and testing him from a distance.

figures.q: a woman in bed

sign.name: Opsign
sign.operation: Locked wide of the two seated across the hearth, the length of the hall between; no move, no cut for as long as the line allows.

key_beat.note: let the singer strike up a wedding tune

beats.text: Penelope sits opposite Odysseus in silence and studies his face and clothing.
Telemachus rebukes her for hardness; she says she and Odysseus share private signs.
Odysseus accepts the delay and turns to the danger from the suitors' families.
He orders the household to create the sound of a wedding so the deaths remain hidden.

figures.q: a seated woman staring

sign.name: Theatrical figure
sign.operation: Frontal wide of the dancers and Phemius; cut outside to a neighbour hearing it in the street.

key_beat.note: no other wife would sit across the room

beats.text: Odysseus bathes while Athena restores his stature and beauty.
Phemius plays the lyre and the household dances so neighbors believe a wedding is underway.
Odysseus returns radiant, but Penelope still refuses immediate recognition.
The king accuses her heart of being harder than stone.

figures.q: a man playing a lyre
dancers in a ring

sign.name: Symbol
sign.operation: Insert of the olive trunk rising through the bed frame, lamp-lit; the same trunk framing as the harbour olive in XIII-S04.

key_beat.note: the summit: she knows him, and says why she could not

beats.text: Penelope orders Eurycleia to move the marriage bed outside the chamber for the stranger.
Odysseus erupts, explaining that he built the bed around a living olive tree and no one could move it intact.
The secret proves identity; Penelope runs to him and embraces him.
She explains that fear of deception caused her delay.
Athena holds back dawn while husband and wife weep and reunite.

figures.q: an olive tree trunk
a carved wooden bed

sign.name: Mise en abyme
sign.operation: Tableaux of the voyage behind the couple.

key_beat.note: one labour is still on me

beats.text: In bed Odysseus and Penelope recount the years they spent apart.
He tells her Tiresias's command to travel inland with an oar and appease Poseidon.
He describes the eventual gentle death foretold for him.
Penelope accepts that further movement remains even after homecoming.
They sleep while Athena finally releases the dawn.

figures.q: a man carrying an oar

sign.name: Any-space-whatever
sign.operation: Empty dark wide of the streets.

key_beat.note: stay within doors, and bar them

beats.text: At dawn Odysseus arms himself with Telemachus, Eumaeus, and Philoetius.
He orders Penelope and the women to remain inside and reveal nothing.
Athena covers the four men in darkness as they leave the city.
They travel toward Laertes's farm before the suitors' deaths become public.

sign.name: Sheets of the past
sign.operation: Long track.

beats.text: Hermes gathers the suitors' shades with his wand and leads them squeaking like bats toward the dead.
They pass Ocean, the White Rock, the Gates of the Sun, and the land of dreams.
In the meadow of asphodel they meet Achilles, Agamemnon, Ajax, and other warriors.
The dead gather to hear how so many noble young men died together.

figures.q: a swarm of bats

sign.name: Powers of the false
sign.operation: Straight testimony close.

beats.text: Agamemnon and Achilles debate the honor of their deaths and funerals.
Amphimedon tells how Penelope delayed the suitors, how Odysseus returned as a beggar, and how the bow contest became slaughter.
Agamemnon praises Penelope's enduring intelligence and condemns Clytemnestra by contrast.
The underworld recognizes Odysseus's household victory as a new song.

sign.name: Bodies of attitude
sign.operation: Static wide in the orchard.

beats.text: Odysseus reaches the farm and finds Laertes alone in patched clothes, tending a tree.
He sends his companions to prepare food and approaches under another false identity.
He claims to have hosted Odysseus years earlier and watches his father collapse in grief.
Unable to continue, Odysseus embraces him and names himself.
Laertes asks for proof beyond desire.

figures.q: an old man with a spade

scenes.title: The Scar and the Orchard Trees

sign.name: Strong destiny
sign.operation: Marked flashback (soft, warm) of the boy and Laertes walking the rows; dissolve back to the old man collapsing into his son's arms.

key_beat.note: count the trees you gave me when I was a boy

beats.text: Odysseus shows the boar scar as physical proof.
He names the thirteen pear trees, ten apple trees, forty fig trees, and fifty vine rows Laertes gave him as a child.
Laertes recognizes the private map of inheritance and collapses into his son's arms.
He fears that Ithaca lacks men willing to defend them from the suitors' kin.

figures.q: a pear tree with fruit
a boy walking in an orchard

sign.name: Limpid and opaque
sign.operation: Medium as he steps from the bath.

beats.text: Laertes is bathed and anointed inside the farmhouse.
Athena makes him taller and stronger, restoring royal presence.
Dolius and his sons return from the fields, recognize Odysseus, and join the feast.
The reunited household eats while rumors of the massacre spread through town.

figures.q: an old man bathing

sign.name: Dividual
sign.operation: Pan across the families.

beats.text: In town the bodies are carried from the palace and each family mourns its dead.
Medon and Phemius testify that a god fought beside Odysseus.
Halitherses reminds the people that he warned them and that their own tolerance enabled the disaster.
Eupithes rejects caution and leads armed relatives toward Laertes's farm.
Some citizens refuse to join and remain behind.

figures.q: mourning women in black

scenes.title: Zeus and Athena Set the Terms

sign.name: Limit of the large form action-image
sign.operation: Two-shot, high space.

beats.text: Athena asks Zeus whether the conflict should continue or peace should be imposed.
Zeus declares that Odysseus may remain king after punishing the suitors.
He orders both sides to forget the bloodshed through oath and renewed prosperity.
Athena descends toward Ithaca to terminate the cycle.

sign.name: Binomial
sign.operation: Wide on one axis.

beats.text: Odysseus sees the armed relatives approaching and distributes weapons among the farm household.
Athena appears as Mentor and urges Laertes's line to prove its strength.
Laertes prays, throws a spear, and kills Eupithes through the helmet.
Odysseus and Telemachus charge the remaining attackers.
The final battle begins to repeat the slaughter that peace must stop.

figures.q: an old man throwing a spear
a soldier in a helmet

sign.name: Limit of the large form action-image
sign.operation: Wide of the two sides on the farm field; the thunderbolt lands between; hold on Odysseus's raised spear lowering.

beats.text: Athena cries out for both sides to stop and tells the Ithacans to disperse without more blood.
Zeus hurls a thunderbolt before her feet, making the command irresistible.
Odysseus attempts one more charge until Athena restrains and redirects him.
She establishes binding oaths between king and people in Mentor's form.
The poem ends with the household restored and the violence converted into civic peace.

figures.q: a tall woman in a helmet
a lightning bolt striking the ground
